record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Call a rational function A of degree at least two tame if the algebraic curve (A(x) − A(y)) / (x − y) = 0 has no irreducible factors of genus 0 or 1, and call A wild otherwise. Describe all wild rational functions.

evidence.quote: Let A be a rational function of degree at least two. We say that A is tame if the algebraic curve (8) A(x) − A(y) / (x − y) = 0 has no factors of genus zero or one. Otherwise, we say that A is wild.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a rational function $A \in \mathbb{C}(z)$ of degree at least two, consider the affine algebraic curve
$$C_A: \frac{A(x) - A(y)}{x - y} = 0.$$
Call $A$ tame if no irreducible component of $C_A$ has geometric genus $0$ or $1$, and call $A$ wild otherwise. Give a complete description (classification) of all wild rational functions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing all wild rational functions appears to be open. Pakovich and collaborators have established partial results: every "special" rational function is wild, and any rational function with a compositional right factor of degree ≥ 2 having genus 0 or 1 is wild. However, no complete classification of wild rational functions has been published.

status_evidence.title: Tame rational functions: Decompositions of iterates and orbit intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Tame rational functions are introduced via the genus condition on the curve (A(x)-A(y))/(x-y)=0; results concern decompositions and orbit intersections, but no full classification of wild functions is given.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results known; complete description of wild rational functions not provided.

status_evidence.title: On amenable semigroups of rational functions (Pakovich)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses tame vs. wild rational functions; notes that special rational functions are wild and tame semigroups exclude them.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions for wildness are given but a complete classification remains unresolved.
